title: Stop Conditions and Budgets
brief: Five overnight tasks. Three are ordinary bug fixes. Two get stuck: one polls a CI job that is hung, one keeps re-reading a 5,000-token log looking for an error that is not there. The loop has no turn cap and no budget, so the stuck runs go until the platform kills them. Stop them gracefully: zero runaways, $0.20 or less per task on average, and the three real fixes still get done.

The three real fixes still get done (success at least 55%)

hints: Open the Hung CI job and the log tasks. How many turns does each run before something stops it, and who stops it?

A loop needs two caps: a turn cap for cheap loops like polling, and a dollar cap for loops where every turn re-reads something big. Keep both loose enough that a normal fix (about 5 turns, about $0.05) never hits them.
Loop: Max turns 15, Max $ per task 0.25.
explain: A turn cap stops the cheap poll loop; a budget stops the log loop whose context grows by 5,000 tokens a turn. Both end as a graceful stop with a report, not a 60-turn runaway.
